She randomly selected 150 students from all first-year piano students at conservatories in Austria. Each selected student reported their average daily practice time and then completed a sight-reading test. Students who practiced more tended to score higher.
choices: Only the 150 first-year piano students in the sample
All first-year piano students at conservatories in Austria
All piano students, any year, at conservatories in Austria
All first-year music students at conservatories in Austria
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from all first-year piano students at Austrian conservatories. Because the selection was random, the results reach exactly that group, with all three qualifiers kept: first-year, piano, and Austrian conservatories.

A.why: You ignored the fact that the students were randomly selected. Random selection is exactly what lets a sample speak for the larger group it came from, so the results are not limited to the 150 students.

C.why: You dropped the 'first-year' qualifier. Students in later years were never part of the group the sample was drawn from, so the results can't be extended to them.

D.why: You dropped the 'piano' qualifier. Only piano students could have been selected, so the results say nothing about students of other instruments or voice.

All adult learners of Japanese at the Toronto school
All adult learners of Japanese in the city of Toronto
All adult learners of Japanese in every country

D.why: You chose the most impressive-sounding group. Volunteers from one school can't represent learners everywhere, especially since nobody was randomly selected.
